I was born in a drouth year. That summer

my mother waited in the house, enclosed

in the sun and the dry ceaseless wind,

for the men to come back in the evenings,

bringing water from a distant spring.

veins of leaves ran dry, roots shrank.

And all my life I have dreaded the return

of that year, sure that it still is

somewhere, like a dead enemys soul.

Fear of dust in my mouth is always with me,

and I am the faithful husband of the rain,

I love the water of wells and springs

and the taste of roofs in the water of cisterns.

I am a dry man whose thirst is praise

of clouds, and whose mind is something of a cup.

My sweetness is to wake in the night

after days of dry heat, hearing the rain.

Probably an oversimplification/misunderstanding on my part, but: Employment-at-will. They can fire you at any time just like you can quit at any time, unless you have a contract that says otherwise. I sucks to get fired for something like an unpopular opinion, but if they cannot prove wrongdoing on your part (at least in the US) you'll probably qualify for benefits while you look for another job. If I were fired due to an unpopular opinion, I'd see it as a blessing. I don't want to work in an environment like that.

You would think you'd be grateful but if you happen to love your job even if its a shifty environment then it truly does suck. I've been there, I did not handle the experience well and now it seems as though I am blacklisted from my industry. The best possible thing to do is to just let it go and move on. I feel for ya, it's a horrible position to find yourself in.

If the opinion has an effect on the work then that is completely understandable. Also, if the person is unduely vocal about the opinion and is causing a disturbance because of it, it is understandable.
